title: Hybrid Telerehabilitation for Anterior Knee Pain in Routine Physiotherapy Practice
official: Integrating Hybrid Telerehabilitation Into Routine Physiotherapy Practice for Anterior Knee Pain: Protocol for a Real-World Pragmatic Mixed-Methods Study
summary:
This study will examine how hybrid telerehabilitation is used in routine physiotherapy care for adults with anterior knee pain. Approximately 30 participants will be followed for 72 weeks while receiving individualized treatment from their physiotherapist, supported by the moveUP mobile application. The application provides prescribed exercises, educational information, communication with the physiotherapist, and progress monitoring.

The study will assess adherence to rehabilitation, pain, knee function, quality of life, psychological factors, and physical activity. It will also explore whether patient adherence and physiotherapist engagement are associated with clinical outcomes. Interviews with patients and healthcare professionals will examine barriers and facilitators to using the platform in routine care.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age 18 years or older.
* Clinical diagnosis of anterior knee pain, including patellofemoral pain, patellar tendinopathy, Hoffa's fat pad syndrome, chondromalacia, or femoropatellar, tibiopatellar, or tibiofemoral osteoarthritis not requiring surgery.
* Access to a smartphone compatible with the moveUP application.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Currently awaiting spine or lower-limb surgery.
* Lower-limb surgery or other invasive intervention within the previous two years.
* Joint prosthesis.
* Acute trauma to the trunk or lower limbs, or fracture, dislocation, or other musculoskeletal pathology of the affected lower limb within the previous six months.
* Saphenous nerve neuritis or Ehlers-Danlos syndrome.
* Severe osteoarthritis requiring joint replacement, systemic inflammatory joint disease (including rheumatoid arthritis or gout), or joint infection.
* Persistent low back pain lasting three months or longer.
* Vascular, respiratory, or neurological conditions that interfere with participation.
* Cognitive or psychiatric impairment limiting application use or communication.
* Pregnancy.
